alt: We'd been itching to come here for months, but to be honest, it wasn't quite as good as everyone made out.
point: 惦记了好几个月 → had been dying to；名不副实 → didn't live up to

zh: 不好意思，我们的甜点可能被漏掉了？点了快半小时了，不着急，就是确认一下。
en: Sorry, I think our desserts might have slipped through the cracks. We ordered them about half an hour ago. No rush, just checking.
alt: Sorry to bother you, but I wonder if our desserts got missed? We ordered about half an hour ago. No hurry at all.
point: 委婉推测 → might have slipped through the cracks；ago → ordered

zh: 这顿本来该我请的，结果你又趁我不注意先把账结了。
en: I was going to shout you dinner, but you've gone and paid the bill again before I had a chance.
alt: Dinner was supposed to be on me, but you've snuck off and paid again before I could.
point: 本来要 → was going to；口语“又…了”→ you've gone and done

zh: 我也不是要你马上还钱，只是咱们当时说好月底的，现在都过去两周了。
en: I'm not saying you need to pay me back right away, but we did say the end of the month, and that was two weeks ago.
alt: There's no huge rush, but we agreed on the end of the month, and that's been and gone by two weeks.
point: 强调当时说过 → did say；那是两周前 → that was two weeks ago

zh: 那封邮件里的链接我差一点就点了，幸好想起来之前听说过一模一样的骗局。
en: I was this close to clicking the link in that email, but luckily I remembered hearing about a scam just like it.
alt: I very nearly clicked the link in that email, but thankfully I'd heard about a scam exactly like it.
point: 差一点就 → was this close to；想起听说过 → remembered hearing

zh: 照这样下去，到明年这个时候，车贷应该就还清了，我们也能喘口气了。
en: If we keep this up, by this time next year we'll have paid off the car loan and can finally breathe a bit easier.
alt: At this rate, we'll have cleared the car loan by this time next year, and things will feel a lot less tight.
point: 到将来某时已还清 → will have paid off；if 从句用现在时

zh: 我在线上排队排了四十分钟，系统突然叫我改天再试，你说离谱不离谱。
en: I'd been sitting in the online queue for forty minutes when it told me to try again another day. You couldn't make it up.
alt: After forty minutes in the online queue, it just told me to come back another day. Unbelievable.
point: 之前一直在排 → had been sitting…when + 过去时

zh: 我可能哪儿填错了，因为交上去以后就一点消息都没有，八成卡在哪个环节了。
en: I might have filled something in wrong, because I haven't heard a peep since I submitted it. It could well be stuck somewhere.
alt: Maybe I got something wrong on the form, since there's been total silence since I sent it in. It's probably stuck in the system.
point: 可能填错了 → might have filled；交了以后没消息 → haven't heard since

zh: 既然我们邮件来来回回好几周了，要不直接打个电话把这事说清楚？
en: Seeing as we've been going back and forth by email for weeks, would it be easier to just jump on a call and sort it out?
alt: Since we've been emailing back and forth for weeks now, shall we just have a quick call and get it sorted?
point: 来来回回好几周 → have been going back and forth

zh: 也许是我想多了，但我觉得这颗痣最近好像大了一点。
en: It might just be me being paranoid, but I think this mole's got a bit bigger lately.
alt: I could be imagining it, but this mole seems to have grown a little recently.
point: 最近变大了 → has got bigger lately；也许是我多心 → might just be me

zh: 我原以为只是普通扭伤，就没当回事继续走路，结果拍片才知道其实骨折了。
en: I'd assumed it was just a sprain and kept walking on it, but the X-ray showed I'd actually broken it.
alt: I thought it was only a sprain so I carried on as normal, but it turned out on the X-ray that it was broken.
point: 原以为 → had assumed；片子显示早就断了 → showed I'd broken

zh: 医生这几年一直劝我少喝咖啡，我也确实在努力，至于进展嘛，就说是“循序渐进”吧。
en: My GP's been telling me to cut back on coffee for years, and I have been trying. Progress has been, let's say, gradual.
alt: My doctor's been on at me to drink less coffee for years, and I am trying, but progress has been slow, shall we say.
point: 一直在劝 → has been telling；强调确实在 → I have been trying

zh: 我还以为是谁在放烟花，出去一看才发现对面的车库着火了。
en: I thought someone was letting off fireworks, but when I went outside, I realised the garage across the road had caught fire.
alt: I assumed it was fireworks, but when I stepped outside I saw the garage over the road was on fire.
point: 以为正在 → thought…was letting off；发现已着火 → had caught fire

zh: 幸亏地震前一个月我们刚把书架固定在墙上，不然真不敢想会怎么样。
en: Thank goodness we'd bolted the bookshelves to the wall a month before the quake. I hate to think what would have happened otherwise.
alt: Luckily we'd fixed the bookcases to the wall a month before the earthquake, or who knows what would've happened.
point: 地震前已固定 → had bolted；不然会 → would have happened

zh: 你们现在应该已经到家了吧？我刚听说你们那边因为洪水封路了。
en: You'll be home by now, I hope? I've just heard they've closed the road out your way because of flooding.
alt: I hope you've made it home by now. I've just heard the road out your way's been closed with the flooding.
point: 推测现在 → You'll be home by now；刚听说 → have just heard

zh: 我开了二十年车，一张罚单都没吃过，结果上周在学校门口被测速相机拍了。
en: I'd gone twenty years without a single ticket, and then last week I got snapped by a speed camera outside a school.
alt: Twenty years without a ticket, and then a speed camera caught me outside a school last week.
point: 那之前保持了二十年 → had gone twenty years without

zh: 这辆车都快跑了三十万公里了，我看也撑不了多久了。
en: This car's done nearly three hundred thousand kilometres, so I doubt it's got much life left in it.
alt: This car's clocked almost 300,000 km, so I can't see it lasting much longer.
point: 里程数 → has done…kilometres，用完成时

zh: 等你赶到，我估计已经在路边等了一个小时了，所以别着急，慢慢开，注意安全。
en: By the time you get here, I'll probably have been waiting on the roadside for an hour, so there's no point rushing. Drive safely.
alt: I'll have been sitting on the side of the road for an hour by the time you arrive, so take your time and drive carefully.
point: 到那时已等了一小时 → will have been waiting

zh: 我们本来想来一场说走就走的旅行，结果光比较酒店价格就花了三个周末。
en: We'd meant it to be a spontaneous trip, but we've ended up spending three weekends comparing hotel prices.
alt: It was supposed to be a spur-of-the-moment trip, and yet we've spent three weekends comparing hotels.
point: 本来想 → had meant；结果到现在 → have ended up spending

zh: 要不是你提醒我查护照，我现在估计还在值机柜台跟人吵呢。
en: If you hadn't reminded me to check my passport, I'd probably still be at the check-in counter arguing with someone right now.
alt: Without your reminder about my passport, I'd most likely be stuck at check-in having an argument right now.
point: 过去没发生 + 现在的结果 → If you hadn't…, I'd still be

zh: 这趟旅行我们计划了快两年，下个月这时候我们就在意大利吃冰淇淋了，到现在还觉得不真实。
en: We've been planning this trip for nearly two years, and this time next month we'll be eating gelato in Italy. I still can't quite believe it.
alt: We've been planning this for almost two years, and in a month we'll be having gelato in Italy. It still doesn't feel real.
point: 计划了两年 → have been planning；下个月这时 → will be eating

zh: 他们说这条路线“很轻松”，我现在开始怀疑写这话的人到底有没有走过。
en: They said this track was 'an easy stroll', and I'm starting to wonder whether whoever wrote that has ever actually walked it.
alt: Apparently this track is 'an easy walk', and I'm beginning to doubt the person who said that has ever done it.
point: 有没有走过 → has ever walked；开始怀疑 → I'm starting to wonder

zh: 预报说今天放晴，结果我们刚出发就下起了大雨，惠灵顿的天气就是这样。
en: The forecast promised sunshine, and we'd barely set off when it started chucking it down. Typical Wellington, really.
alt: Sunshine, the forecast said. We'd hardly left before it started pouring. Classic Wellington.
point: 刚…就 → had barely set off when；大雨 → chucking it down

zh: 我以为涂了防晒就没事了，根本没意识到自己已经在太阳底下待了四个小时。
en: I thought I'd be fine with sunscreen on, but I hadn't realised I'd been out in the sun for four hours.
alt: I figured sunscreen would do the trick, but I didn't clock that I'd been out in the sun for four hours.
point: 以为会 → thought I'd be；没意识到已经 → hadn't realised I'd been

zh: 我们队已经连输六场了，说实话，周六要是能达阵一次，大家都会高兴坏了。
en: We've lost six on the trot, so honestly, if we even score a try on Saturday, we'll be over the moon.
alt: We've lost six in a row, so if we manage a single try on Saturday, we'll be absolutely stoked.
point: 连输六场 → have lost six on the trot；if 从句用现在时

zh: 我以前一周能跑五十公里，自从膝盖受伤，现在能跑五公里就谢天谢地了。
en: I used to clock fifty kilometres a week, but since I did my knee, I'm lucky if I manage five.
alt: I used to run fifty k a week, but ever since I hurt my knee, five is a good day.
point: 以前常 → used to；自从受伤 → since I did my knee（过去时）

zh: 他说“就去打一小会儿高尔夫”，这都六个小时过去了。
en: He said he was 'just popping out for a quick round of golf', and that was six hours ago.
alt: He told me he'd only be out for a quick round of golf, and that was six hours ago.
point: 转述 → said he was popping out；那是六小时前 → that was six hours ago

zh: 这本书我一直想看，可每次一拿起来，没翻几页就睡着了。
en: I've been meaning to read that book for ages, but every time I pick it up, I'm asleep within a few pages.
alt: I've wanted to read that book for ages, but whenever I start it, I nod off after a couple of pages.
point: 一直想（还没做）→ have been meaning to；每次 → 一般现在时

zh: 你应该已经看完大结局了吧？我不剧透，但我到现在还没从那个结局里缓过来。
en: You'll have seen the finale by now, surely? I won't give anything away, but I still haven't got over that ending.
alt: I assume you've watched the finale by now? No spoilers, but I'm still not over that ending.
point: 推测已看 → You'll have seen；还没缓过来 → still haven't got over

zh: 告诉你，我年轻的时候吉他弹得可好了，只不过现在手指不太听使唤了。
en: I'll have you know I used to play a mean guitar, though these days my fingers don't quite cooperate.
alt: Believe it or not, I used to be pretty handy on the guitar, but my fingers aren't what they were.
point: 以前会 → used to；幽默地“告诉你” → I'll have you know

zh: 我们说要聚一聚说了快一年了，这次一定要把日子定下来。
en: We've been saying we'll catch up for about a year now, so let's actually put a date in the diary this time.
alt: We've been promising to get together for nearly a year, so let's pin down a date this time.
point: 说了快一年 → have been saying we'll；这次真的 → let's actually

zh: 我本来不打算说的，但你那天在派对上讲的那个笑话，好像让Amy有点不舒服。
en: I wasn't going to say anything, but I think that joke you made at the party might have rubbed Amy up the wrong way.
alt: I wasn't planning to mention it, but your joke at the party may have upset Amy a little.
point: 本来不打算 → wasn't going to；可能惹到了 → might have rubbed

zh: 你上次见面的时候说要请我喝咖啡，别以为我忘了。
en: You said you'd shout me a coffee last time we caught up, and don't think for a second I've forgotten.
alt: Last time we met you promised to buy me a coffee, and I haven't forgotten, just so you know.
point: 转述承诺 → said you'd；别以为我忘了 → don't think I've forgotten

zh: 我不想扫兴，但我们去年也说圣诞节简单过，结果花的钱比哪年都多。
en: I don't want to be a killjoy, but we said we'd keep Christmas low-key last year too, and we ended up spending more than ever.
alt: Not to be a party pooper, but last year we also agreed on a quiet Christmas and still spent more than we ever have.
point: 去年说过要 → said we'd；结果 → ended up spending

zh: 等到办婚礼那天，他俩就在一起十二年了，也真该修成正果了。
en: By the time the wedding comes round, they'll have been together for twelve years, so it's well and truly about time.
alt: They'll have been together twelve years by the wedding day, so it's about time, really.
point: 到那时已在一起 → will have been together；by the time 后用现在时

zh: 我筹划这个惊喜好几个星期了，结果我女儿一不小心说漏了嘴。
en: I'd been planning the surprise for weeks, and then my daughter went and let the cat out of the bag.
alt: I'd spent weeks planning the surprise, and then my daughter accidentally gave the game away.
point: 之前一直在筹划 → had been planning；说漏嘴 → let the cat out of the bag

zh: 我妈老说她“过几天就走”，这话她都说了三个月了。
en: Mum keeps saying she'll be heading home 'in a few days', and she's been saying that for three months.
alt: My mum's been telling us she's leaving 'in a few days' for three months now.
point: 老说 → keeps saying she'll be；说了三个月 → has been saying

zh: 他信誓旦旦说作业几个小时前就写完了，可我刚看了一眼，一个字都没动。
en: He swore blind he'd finished his homework hours ago, but I've just had a look and he hasn't written a single word.
alt: He insisted he'd done his homework ages ago, but I've just checked and there's not a word on the page.
point: 他说已经 → swore he'd finished；刚看了 → have just had a look

zh: 说起来，我小时候也是这么跟我妈顶嘴的，现在才明白她当年有多不容易。
en: To be fair, I used to talk back to my mum in exactly the same way, and only now am I realising how hard it must have been for her.
alt: Mind you, I used to answer back to my mum just like that, and I'm only now seeing how tough it must have been for her.
point: 以前常 → used to；对过去的推测 → must have been

zh: 猫好像认定新沙发是它的了，自从我们搬回家，它就一直在上面磨爪子。
en: The cat seems to have decided the new couch belongs to her. She's been sharpening her claws on it ever since we brought it home.
alt: The cat has clearly claimed the new sofa. She's been using it as a scratching post since the day it arrived.
point: 好像已经认定 → seems to have decided；从那以后一直 → has been…ever since

zh: 我本来只是帮朋友照看一个周末，那都是三年前的事了，现在它彻底成了我们家的。
en: I was only supposed to be minding him for a weekend, and that was three years ago. He's well and truly ours now.
alt: I was just meant to look after him for one weekend, three years ago. He's definitely ours now.
point: 本来只是 → was only supposed to be；那是三年前 → that was

zh: 要是早知道小狗这么能拆家，我当初可能会再三考虑，不过现在给我什么我都不换。
en: If I'd known how much damage a puppy could do, I might have thought twice. Then again, I wouldn't swap him for anything.
alt: Had I known what a puppy could destroy, I might have reconsidered, but I wouldn't trade him for the world.
point: 早知道 → If I'd known；可能会 → might have thought twice

zh: 我不是故意不回你消息，那几天我状态特别差，什么都不想面对。
en: I wasn't ignoring you on purpose. I'd been in a pretty bad place for a few days and just couldn't face anything.
alt: I didn't mean to go quiet on you. I'd been struggling for a few days and couldn't deal with anything.
point: 当时不是故意 → wasn't ignoring；那之前一直 → had been in a bad place

zh: 我知道你最近经历了很多，如果你想聊聊，我随时都在，别有压力。
en: I know you've been going through a lot lately, so if you ever want to talk, I'm here, no pressure.
alt: I know things have been really hard for you lately. If you need to talk, I'm around, no pressure at all.
point: 最近一直在经历 → have been going through；if 从句用现在时

zh: 那么多年我一直在怪自己，直到最近才慢慢接受，有些事本来就不是我能控制的。
en: For years I'd blamed myself, and it's only recently that I've come to accept that some things were never in my control.
alt: I spent years blaming myself, and only lately have I accepted that some of it was never up to me.
point: 过去多年 → had blamed；最近才接受 → have come to accept
